sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from a full-data law with consistency and conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units with \(X\in\mathbb T^d\), binary treatment, and outcomes in the standard Borel space \(\mathcal Y\); two-outcome laws are used only as least-favorable submodels.
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown Hölder propensity \(e\) with fixed overlap; a comparison experiment supplies \(e\) to the test.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(t>d/2\), the explicit construction uses no preliminary nuisance fit: it estimates arm Gram matrices on deterministic half-samples and applies finite ordered higher-order corrections on the opposite halves. For \(0<t\le d/2\), the distinct block-local collision and occupancy handle remains the proposed route; Wald comparisons additionally require a cross-fitted covariance estimate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives a test with valid type 1 error and consistency against fixed alternatives.
The minimax lower bound is attained by a local polynomial R-Learner under additional design-density conditions.

Version 5 proves semiparametric efficiency without covariate-density smoothness for the scalar mean under missing at random, and extends the construction to a class of scalar doubly robust functionals, using an empirical Gram basis with \(k=o(n)\).
Spectral regularization is minimax optimal with a smaller separation boundary than MMD in direct two-sample testing.
A moderated kernel test attains source-class goodness-of-fit rates that ordinary MMD can miss.
MMDAgg is minimax adaptive over Sobolev balls up to an iterated logarithmic term.
Cross-fitted one-step estimators can be efficient for differentiable Hilbert-valued parameters.
A characteristic outcome kernel makes the unsmoothed pointwise conditional discrepancy identify equality of conditional laws.
Random design changes the minimax rate for nonparametric variance estimation.
Occupancy-aware binning attains minimax conditional-independence testing rates under smooth conditional laws.

body.tldr: The all-tests SCoDiTE problem has two mathematically separate branches. When \(t>d/2\), a cell-local polynomial empirical higher-order estimator with rank \(M\asymp n^\gamma=o(n)\), a finite Neumann correction, and a common \(K_X\)-anchor has uniform mean-squared error \(O(n^{-1})\) over every bounded positive design density, without smoothness of \(f_X\) or of the feature map. Its deterministic class-oracle variance envelope gives uniform size and root-rate power; a regular constant-contrast path gives the matching lower bound when that path belongs to the class. For \(0<t\le d/2\), the separate collision and occupancy handle remains unchanged: the legal fuzzy construction proves the slower uniform-design lower radius \(n^{-2t/(2t+d)}\) for \(0<s\le1/2\), while the arbitrary-density match, spectral method classification, and adaptive grid remain open. Characteristicness of the outcome kernel does not turn the covariate-smoothed null into pointwise conditional homogeneity.

project_justification.gap: Existing SCoDiTE theory is first order and pointwise in the law, direct spectral tests omit causal nuisances, and scalar empirical higher-order results do not establish a Hilbert-valued common-anchor expansion or a uniform SCoDiTE test. Below the smoothness elbow, no checked result matches the legal fuzzy lower experiment under an arbitrary bounded design density.
project_justification.niche: The paper proves only the density-robust high-smoothness root-rate theorem. It leaves the rough-design all-tests modulus unresolved and separately leaves unresolved whether identity or resolvent weighting attains that unknown modulus.
project_justification.fill: Above the elbow, a separate explicit higher-order construction uses cell-local polynomial spans, stabilized arm Gram matrices, finite Neumann chains, and two one-sided plus one common-anchor correction. Their exact inclusion--exclusion identity leaves the product of the propensity and arm-embedding projection residuals while evaluating \(K_X\) exactly, which yields uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) Hilbert risk and oracle-calibrated testing. The original collision and occupancy handle is retained only for the rough branch, where the paired exact-null tables and fuzzy lower bound feed the unresolved arbitrary-density frontier and its spectral and adaptive consumers.

body.related_work: Jain and Luedtke (2026) define the SCoDiTE moment, its efficient Hilbert influence function, and fixed-operator MMD and Wald tests; their first-order product-rate theory does not supply the higher-order uniform test proved here. Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2026, arXiv:1705.07577v5) prove semiparametric efficiency without density smoothness for scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals using empirical Gram bases with rank \(o(n)\). The high-smoothness theorem adapts that architecture through an explicit common-anchor inclusion--exclusion correction and proves its risk directly; it does not import a scalar theorem. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) motivate the localized fuzzy-hypothesis architecture in the separate rough branch, whose nonfactorizing alternative table is specific to the SCoDiTE null. Direct-sample weighting results under different metrics and direct-sample aggregation templates do not settle any of the three remaining questions here: the rough arbitrary-density modulus, method optimality relative to that unknown modulus, or adaptive calibration.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The high-smoothness test is calibrated by the deterministic envelope \(V_\star\), whose finiteness is proved uniformly but whose numerical value is a class-oracle constant rather than a data-derived critical value. This suffices for the minimax existence and size theorem but is not yet a practical calibration recipe. In the early-kill rough case \(d=1\) and \(\beta_e=\beta_m=0.2\), the nominal uniform-design partition has \(K_h\asymp n^{10/9}>n\), outside both the proved high-smoothness construction and the scalar empirical-HOIF regime. The remaining audit is therefore still the rough arbitrary-density upper procedure and its match to a primitive occupancy functional. The two-outcome family is only a least-favorable proof device; an attaining rough procedure must handle the multivariate wealth outcome.
body.honest_scope: The density-robust root-rate upper theorem is proved for \(t>d/2\) by an explicit finite-order Hilbert-valued estimator with \(M=o(n)\). Its matching root-rate lower bound, and hence equality, is conditional on the stated nondegenerate quadratic-mean differentiable constant-contrast path. The calibration envelope is deterministic and finite but oracle. The known-propensity benchmark, corrected rough uniform-design fuzzy lower branch, and Fourier quotient-null result remain separate established or posed components. For \(0<t\le d/2\), the collision and occupancy handle has not been replaced: the arbitrary-density equivalence, the spectral iff classification, and the adaptive regularization grid remain open. No claim is made that \(K_h>n\) itself proves an occupancy penalty or that characteristic constituent kernels make the smoothed null identical to conditional homogeneity.
